Key candidates:

1. **`inProgressNodes` uses `gh issue list --label`** — `gh issue list` excludes pull requests? Actually no: `gh issue list` in the search API returns both issues and PRs when using `--search`, but with GraphQL `repository.issues` it returns only issues (PullRequests are separate in GraphQL... actually `repository.issues` in GraphQL does NOT include pull requests; GitHub's GraphQL `issues` connection is issues only). Hmm — with `--label`, gh uses searchIssues which passes `type:issue`? SearchQueryBuild sets `Type: options.Entity` = "issue", so `type:issue`. So PRs wearing in-progress would NOT be listed. That's a real gap: the sweep only examines issues, not pull requests. The watch's reconcile handles PRs. A PR whose runner run died mid-work keeps `atomaton/in-progress` and a claim, and the sweep would never see it. Is that merge-blocking? The issue's scope says "候補 node の列挙(in-progress label の付いた issue/PR を検索するのが自然 — 手段は engineer 選択)". PRs are explicitly named in the scope. And PRs hold claims: `create_pr`... well, agent runs on PRs (reviewer runs on PRs) take a turn and claim. So a reviewer run dying mid-work on a PR leaves a stale claim on the PR, and the sweep can't see it. That's a real coverage defect against the acceptance criteria "「run が終了済みで未 release の claim」を持つ node が、sweep によって release される". Hmm, but is it truly that `gh issue list` excludes PRs? Let me verify. With `--label` filter, gh's `issueList` calls `searchIssues` with `filters.Entity = "issue"` and `filters.Repo`. `SearchQueryBuild` sets `Type: options.Entity` → "issue" → produces `type:issue`. Hmm, wait — but gh issue list with `--label` uses searchIssues... Actually adding `--label` triggers the search path (see `issueList` in list.go: if filters.Search != "" || len(filters.Labels) > 0 → searchIssues). And searchIssues sets `filters.Entity = "issue"` → type:issue qualifier. So yes, PRs are excluded.

Wait, but hold on. In newer gh versions, `gh issue list` search uses advanced issue search and might not add type:issue... The code shows `filters.Entity = "issue"`, and SearchQueryBuild sets `Type: options.Entity` = "issue". So `type:issue` is in the query. Therefore pull requests are excluded from results.

Hmm, but does the repo rely on that elsewhere? `report_config_findings` uses issue list with search for a marker. Fine.

So finding #1: the sweep enumerates only issues, not PRs, though the design says node = issue or PR. Reviewer runs on PRs leave claims on the PR. So a stale claim on a PR is never released by the sweep. That is a genuine functional gap w.r.t. acceptance criterion 2 (release stale claims) — although acceptance criteria say "node" generally; the sweep test only covers issues. Is it merge-blocking? The issue statement says the guard must not delete under a stale lock (tested), and the sweep releases stale claims. For PRs there's an additional path: the guard now keeps the comment on a stale lock, and the reviewer can be re-invoked by a comment. So the lock is not permanently stuck on a PR — a person's comment survives. But the in-progress label stays and... hmm, does the guard's keep mean the comment goes to dispatch? On manual-comment workflow, guardStep returns blocked=false, then dispatch proceeds, so a new run dispatches on the PR and claims the turn. So the PR is reachable. But the sweep's promise "release stale claims on the nodes" is partially unmet. And importantly the issue explicitly says 候補 node の列挙(in-progress label の付いた issue/PR). I should verify `gh issue list` behavior more concretely before claiming. Let me check whether there's an existing test in the repo asserting `gh issue list` includes PRs... unclear. Actually a cleaner check: does `gh issue list --search` fetch `type:issue`? Yes from source I read.

Hmm, but careful: In recent gh versions with advanced issue search, `--label` might use `is:issue`. Either way, PRs excluded.

Let me be careful about how strongly to claim. I could report it as a finding with the evidence: `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts:119-123` uses `gh issue list`, and `gh`'s issue listing passes `type:issue` (gh source), so PRs are never examined — yet runs do take turns on PRs (reviewer), and a dead reviewer run leaves the same claim. Correction: enumerate PRs too (e.g. `gh pr list --label ...`) or use `gh api search/issues` with `is:issue is:pr` OR-ed... Hmm. Actually a simpler correction: use `gh search issues --label X --state open --include-prs`? Hmm, `gh search issues` has no --include-prs... `gh search prs`. Alternatively use `gh api search/issues?q=repo:...+label:...+is:open` which returns both issues and PRs (is:open without type). That's the natural fix.

Is this within the mandatory checks? It's a correctness/coverage defect against acceptance criteria. I think it's a legitimate merge-blocking finding, but I should be careful: is it possible that PR-side claims don't matter? Let's check: what labels does a PR wear? `atomaton/in-progress` is applied by runner's "Add atomaton/in-progress label (the turn is with a run)" step for both issues and PRs (`gh issue edit` works on PRs). And reviewer runs on PRs claim the turn with the ask being waiting comment etc. So yes PRs can hold stale claims. In fact the PR under review itself (#469) wears `atomaton/in-progress` and was opened by an engineer run that died — that's exactly a stale claim on... wait, that's a PR. The issue #462 also wears in-progress.

Hmm, this is interesting: the harm in the issue's own narrative (#12 run died) was on an issue. But #469 is a PR wearing in-progress.

2. **`readRunStatus` uses `ghRead` with `--jq ".status"`** and treats only `completed` as stale. Note GitHub's run status values: `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `requested`, `waiting`, `pending`. For a run that was *cancelled* or failed, status is still `completed`. OK.

But there is a subtle severe issue: **the run id in the claim is the runner run id; for a run dispatched with `workflow_dispatch`, `actions/runs/{id}` needs `actions: read` permission.** The workflow permissions `ATOMATON_WORKFLOW_PERMISSIONS` includes `actions: write` — fine. Unless the last event is a waiting from... hmm, events are per entry. If `events[last] === "waiting"`, the entry that produced it is the newest waiting. So fine.

§4 of #441.

## The harm this removes

Every runner run is dispatched by the machinery with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub starts no
workflow run for an event its own token triggered — so `Atomaton Run Watch`'s
`workflow_run: completed` trigger has only ever fired for ENTRY runs. Measured over its
whole history, zero reconciliations were of a runner run. The outside check was pointed
away from the runs it exists for.

The #12 run that died on its context budget is the state that follows: a claim
(`atomaton:took=55 run=<dead>`) with no ending after it. Every reader treats a claim alone as
"an agent is working", so the guard deleted the person's `/atomaton recover` twice, and
nothing could heal the thread from inside. A park (`atomaton:ended=waiting`) whose
aggregation never arrived is the same jam one step later.

## What changed

**One judgement, `src/domain/work/stale-lock.ts`.** Run facts are primary: the claim names
the run that took it, and GitHub says whether that run finished. `completed` + no release is
the whole of "nobody is coming", with no timer. Timers exist only where a run cannot answer —
`CLAIM_WITHOUT_RUN_MINUTES = 360` for a claim naming no run, `PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30`
for a park's grace (a park's run has always finished by definition, so the run fact says
nothing about whether the collection is still coming).

Only the answered `"completed"` reads as stale; every other or unread status is fresh or
unknown. An unreadable run never resolves to stale — that direction deletes a live run's
comments and hands a live run's node to a person.

**The sweep, `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts` + `sweep_stale_locks.ts`.** Of the
open nodes wearing `atomaton/in-progress`, release the ones whose lock is stale. The release
is the same turn-ending the per-run watch posts (`ended=done answers=<ask> run=<sweep run>`),
so the guard, the aggregation and the next sweep all read the thread as healed. Parks get
their own wording — "the resume … never arrived", never "no answer was posted", which would be
false. Each release is proven by re-reading the thread; a release that did not take is the one
state worth a red run (the node then carries a comment claiming a return beside a thread that
denies it). Nothing stale ⇒ no writes at all.

**The guard, `guard_comment_during_run.ts`.** `commentWouldBeRemoved` now returns the lock it
judged on — the claim with its comment's `created_at`, and the park's time and ask — both
already parsed and discarded. Under a stale lock the comment is kept, which also lets the
dispatch take it up: the way back in. `abandonedClaim` is deliberately narrower than
`lockVerdict`: a park is never abandoned by the guard, because the aggregation resumes it and
reads what was written during the wait — the sweep releases a missed one.

**The schedule, `atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts`.** `schedule: [{ cron: "*/15 * * * *" }]` beside the
existing trigger, a separate `sweep` job (15-minute limit, not the usual 5), and each job gated
to its own event. The concurrency group now names the event as well as the node: a schedule
carries no `workflow_run.display_title`, so without it every sweep would share a group with any
blank-titled watch — and GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so the sweeps would cancel
each other instead of queueing.

`parkExit` is unchanged, with the reason recorded at `request_stop.ts:132`: it sees one node's
thread and nothing about whether the run it names is still going, so widening it would be a
second, worse-informed spelling of the same judgement.

  pre-existing E2E suite.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run lint` clean (typecheck + synth).

## スコープ

1. **schedule 化**: watch wac に `schedule:` cron を追加(workflow_run は維持)。既定値の目安は 15 分ごと(理由を添えれば変更可)。schedule 実行では run-id/display-title が渡らないため、reconcile に sweep モード(例: `--sweep`)を渡す引数の組み立てを wac 側で行う。concurrency は schedule では直列化される group にする。

5. **no-op の安さ**: sweep は stale が無いとき一切書き込まない(読み取りのみ)。release の後のスレッド再読み込みでは open claim が解けていること(自己検証)。

- guard は stale な lock のもとでは人のコメントを削除しない(新テストで固定)。新鮮な lock では現行どおり削除する(既存テストが通る)。

- version bump とリリースはしない。

PR #469: Schedule the run watch, sweep dead claims and parks, and stop the guard deleting under a stale lock
**Labels:** atomaton/waiting-for-person
**Linked Issue:** #462

/reviewer

Part of #462
§4 of #441.

## The harm this removes

Every runner run is dispatched by the machinery with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub starts no
workflow run for an event its own token triggered — so `Atomaton Run Watch`'s
`workflow_run: completed` trigger has only ever fired for ENTRY runs. Measured over its
whole history, zero reconciliations were of a runner run. The outside check was pointed
away from the runs it exists for.

The #12 run that died on its context budget is the state that follows: a claim
(`atomaton:took=55 run=<dead>`) with no ending after it. Every reader treats a claim alone as
"an agent is working", so the guard deleted the person's `/atomaton recover` twice, and
nothing could heal the thread from inside. A park (`atomaton:ended=waiting`) whose
aggregation never arrived is the same jam one step later.

## What changed

**One judgement, `src/domain/work/stale-lock.ts`.** Run facts are primary: the claim names
the run that took it, and GitHub says whether that run finished. `completed` + no release is
the whole of "nobody is coming", with no timer. Timers exist only where a run cannot answer —
`CLAIM_WITHOUT_RUN_MINUTES = 360` for a claim naming no run, `PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30`
for a park's grace (a park's run has always finished by definition, so the run fact says
nothing about whether the collection is still coming).

Only the answered `"completed"` reads as stale; every other or unread status is fresh or
unknown. An unreadable run never resolves to stale — that direction deletes a live run's
comments and hands a live run's node to a person.

**The sweep, `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts` + `sweep_stale_locks.ts`.** Of the
open nodes wearing `atomaton/in-progress`, release the ones whose lock is stale. The release
is the same turn-ending the per-run watch posts (`ended=done answers=<ask> run=<sweep run>`),
so the guard, the aggregation and the next sweep all read the thread as healed. Parks get
their own wording — "the resume … never arrived", never "no answer was posted", which would be
false. Each release is proven by re-reading the thread; a release that did not take is the one
state worth a red run (the node then carries a comment claiming a return beside a thread that
denies it). Nothing stale ⇒ no writes at all.

**The guard, `guard_comment_during_run.ts`.** `commentWouldBeRemoved` now returns the lock it
judged on — the claim with its comment's `created_at`, and the park's time and ask — both
already parsed and discarded. Under a stale lock the comment is kept, which also lets the
dispatch take it up: the way back in. `abandonedClaim` is deliberately narrower than
`lockVerdict`: a park is never abandoned by the guard, because the aggregation resumes it and
reads what was written during the wait — the sweep releases a missed one.

**The schedule, `atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts`.** `schedule: [{ cron: "*/15 * * * *" }]` beside the
existing trigger, a separate `sweep` job (15-minute limit, not the usual 5), and each job gated
to its own event. The concurrency group now names the event as well as the node: a schedule
carries no `workflow_run.display_title`, so without it every sweep would share a group with any
blank-titled watch — and GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so the sweeps would cancel
each other instead of queueing.

`parkExit` is unchanged, with the reason recorded at `request_stop.ts:132`: it sees one node's
thread and nothing about whether the run it names is still going, so widening it would be a
second, worse-informed spelling of the same judgement.

## Verification

- `bun test` — **2236 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail** (2242 across 178 files). The 6 skips are the
  pre-existing E2E suite.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run lint` clean (typecheck + synth).
- `bun run synth` → the generated `.github/workflows/atomaton-run-watch.yml` carries
  `on.schedule`, `concurrency.group: atomaton-run-watch-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ … display_title }}`,
  a `watch` job with `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'`, and a `sweep` job with
  `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'`, `timeout-minutes: 15`, and a step running
  `sweep_stale_locks.ts` with `GITHUB_RUN_ID`/`GITHUB_REPOSITORY` from the environment.
- New tests, by the acceptance criteria:
  - `src/domain/work/stale-lock.test.ts` — 19 pass: finished run ⇒ stale, live/unknown status
    ⇒ fresh, unreadable ⇒ unknown never stale, the timer only where a run cannot answer, a
    park inside grace / with open children / with unreadable children, and the guard's
    narrower rule.
  - `src/entrypoints/machinery/sweep_stale_locks.test.ts` — 10 pass: **stale claim ⇒ released**
    (ending + `waiting-for-person`), **fresh claim ⇒ nothing written at all**, **park ⇒ handed
    back** with its own wording, park held while children are open, unreadable run/thread ⇒
    untouched, idempotent second sweep, and the corrective red run.
  - `src/entrypoints/machinery/guard_comment_during_run.test.ts` — 24 pass: **stale lock ⇒
    comment kept** (not deleted, no notice), live run ⇒ still deleted, unreadable status ⇒
    still deleted, park ⇒ still deleted.
  - `tests/contract/generated-workflows.test.ts` — the schedule, the event-aware group, both
    job gates and the sweep step survive generation.
- Existing suites untouched and green: `reconcile_run_ending`, `request_stop`, `run-report`,
  the adapters, and all 498 contract tests.

## Not established

No live GitHub run of the scheduled workflow exists yet — `schedule` only fires on the default
branch, so the cron could not be observed here. The generated YAML and the script it invokes are
what is verified; the first real sweep is after merge.

No version bump and no release, per the constraint. `dist/` is gitignored and regenerated by
`pretest`.

## The harm this removes

Every runner run is dispatched by the machinery with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub starts no
workflow run for an event its own token triggered — so `Atomaton Run Watch`'s
`workflow_run: completed` trigger has only ever fired for ENTRY runs. Measured over its
whole history, zero reconciliations were of a runner run. The outside check was pointed
away from the runs it exists for.

The #12 run that died on its context budget is the state that follows: a claim
(`atomaton:took=55 run=<dead>`) with no ending after it. Every reader treats a claim alone as
"an agent is working", so the guard deleted the person's `/atomaton recover` twice, and
nothing could heal the thread from inside. A park (`atomaton:ended=waiting`) whose
aggregation never arrived is the same jam one step later.

## What changed

**One judgement, `src/domain/work/stale-lock.ts`.** Run facts are primary: the claim names
the run that took it, and GitHub says whether that run finished. `completed` + no release is
the whole of "nobody is coming", with no timer. Timers exist only where a run cannot answer —
`CLAIM_WITHOUT_RUN_MINUTES = 360` for a claim naming no run, `PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30`
for a park's grace (a park's run has always finished by definition, so the run fact says
nothing about whether the collection is still coming).

Only the answered `"completed"` reads as stale; every other or unread status is fresh or
unknown. An unreadable run never resolves to stale — that direction deletes a live run's
comments and hands a live run's node to a person.

**The sweep, `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts` + `sweep_stale_locks.ts`.** Of the
open nodes wearing `atomaton/in-progress`, release the ones whose lock is stale. The release
is the same turn-ending the per-run watch posts (`ended=done answers=<ask> run=<sweep run>`),
so the guard, the aggregation and the next sweep all read the thread as healed. Parks get
their own wording — "the resume … never arrived", never "no answer was posted", which would be
false. Each release is proven by re-reading the thread; a release that did not take is the one
state worth a red run (the node then carries a comment claiming a return beside a thread that
denies it). Nothing stale ⇒ no writes at all.

**The guard, `guard_comment_during_run.ts`.** `commentWouldBeRemoved` now returns the lock it
judged on — the claim with its comment's `created_at`, and the park's time and ask — both
already parsed and discarded. Under a stale lock the comment is kept, which also lets the
dispatch take it up: the way back in. `abandonedClaim` is deliberately narrower than
`lockVerdict`: a park is never abandoned by the guard, because the aggregation resumes it and
reads what was written during the wait — the sweep releases a missed one.

**The schedule, `atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts`.** `schedule: [{ cron: "*/15 * * * *" }]` beside the
existing trigger, a separate `sweep` job (15-minute limit, not the usual 5), and each job gated
to its own event. The concurrency group now names the event as well as the node: a schedule
carries no `workflow_run.display_title`, so without it every sweep would share a group with any
blank-titled watch — and GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so the sweeps would cancel
each other instead of queueing.

`parkExit` is unchanged, with the reason recorded at `request_stop.ts:132`: it sees one node's
thread and nothing about whether the run it names is still going, so widening it would be a
second, worse-informed spelling of the same judgement.

Ready to merge. All three findings verified fixed in the tree. CI green on head 4a78be7.

But wait — I should be careful and do a genuine re-review of the fix commits, not just check the three findings. The engineer changed the enumeration mechanism (`ghPaginated` on REST issues endpoint). Let me sanity-check that: does `ghPaginated("api", path)` produce the right thing? `ghPaginated` calls `gh(...args, "--paginate")` → `gh api repos/owner/repo/issues?state=open&labels=... --paginate`. That works.

One concern: `gh api` with `--paginate` — for REST it follows Link headers. Fine.

Another: the REST issues endpoint's `labels` filter. `labels=atomaton/in-progress` — REST accepts comma-separated label names; slashes in label names should be fine URL-encoded. `encodeURIComponent("atomaton/in-progress")` → `atomaton%2Fin-progress`. Hmm, does the REST issues API accept a percent-encoded label? Yes, it's a query parameter value, percent-encoding is standard and correct.

Also `state=open` includes both issues and PRs wearing the label. Good.

Let me also check the `openUnderOf` — it folds children and pullRequests. Note `links.children` for an Issue query...
